title: Hollow takes away the build, not the years since
intention: Hollow's counterfactual is 'this build never happened', not 'this file as it stood at the anchor': when a whole-file revert cannot run in today's tree, hollow takes away only the build commits' own hunks from HEAD's bytes, and says unmeasurable by name when even that cannot apply.
why: BUILDER measured 2026-10-13 on 6890cf7e4053: the anchor 8efd1ba1's domain.py dies at its own import line (store moved since), so the proof printed no teeth, the reading was UNRAN, and UNRAN reds the PROVED gate. Removing only the build's hunk by hand redded clause 2, so the proof is load-bearing and the instrument could not see it. A load-bearing proof barred from PROVED by its instrument's blindness is distrust spent on work that earned trust (Law 8), and an UNRAN that is really 'the anchor is months old' is an error collapsed into a reading (Law 7).
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the instrument must be able to build the hollow) and Law 3 (a reading measures the build, not the drift since).
how: A Haiku builder needs: (a) the place: _revert in cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py and its caller in measure() (~line 1100-1120 where the mark UNRAN/ok/HOLLOW is set); (b) the build commits are already computed (_build_commits / _named_build_commits, anchor dict) — reuse them, do not re-derive; (c) the hunk revert: for each build commit touching rel, newest first, `git -C <repo> show <c> -- <rel>` piped to `git -C <worktree> apply -R`, with env=git_env(); a nonzero apply raises HollowUnmeasurable; (d) the retry is per file: only a file whose reading came back UNRAN after whole-file revert is retried in hunk mode; (e) proof at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow_takes_away_the_build_not_the_years_since.py with teeth 1-5 in scratch repos (pattern: existing hollow scratch-repo proofs in that folder); (f) a commit touching tester code triggers the ~40-min tester reseal — budget for it. Clause 1 of 6890 (database state, not code) is the builder's own call once this exists.
falsifier: RED if after the build, in scratch repos: (1) build commit B adds a checked hunk to f.py, a later commit L changes f.py's import so the anchor's f.py cannot import at HEAD; measure reads the proof 'ok' (redded) with revert_mode 'hunks' for f.py, not UNRAN; (2) same history, proof that does NOT check the hunk reads HOLLOW, not UNRAN; (3) a file whose whole-file revert imports and runs keeps revert_mode 'whole-file' and today's reading (no behaviour change for the common case); (4) a later commit overlapping B's hunk makes reverse-apply fail: measure raises HollowUnmeasurable naming f.py and B, never returns UNRAN; (5) the sealed evidence.hollow carries revert_mode per file; (6) live: `cairn test --hollow 6890cf7e4053` reads clause 2's proof (test_an_out_of_vocabulary_verdict_is_refused_at_the_database) as ok, not UNRAN. Wrong-intent signal: a proof that was correctly measured whole-file changes reading.
watchme: none, because the regression event is the tester reseal fired by cairn/devices/tester/hooks/pre-commit on every commit touching the tester, and clause 6 is read live by 6890cf7e4053's own PROVED crossing
children: none, because it is one fallback inside cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py
